note: Controlled entity types. An entity may only be given a type from this list; anything else is recorded as an ontology extension with a written reason, and QC-04 reports it. Definitions are deliberately narrow so that 'did the paper really say this' has an answer.

entity_types.name: researcher
entity_types.definition: A named person, group, or author collective who did the work or is credited with a claim.
exclude: institutions unless the paper makes the institution the actor

entity_types.name: material
entity_types.definition: A physical substance, sample, structure, or composition that the paper studies, uses, or measures.
exclude: a material named only as an adjective for a method

entity_types.name: method
entity_types.definition: A procedure, instrument technique, treatment, calculation scheme, or workflow used to produce a result.
exclude: a general verb like 'measure' with no technique

entity_types.name: task
entity_types.definition: The scientific objective, question, or application the work addresses.

entity_types.name: metric
entity_types.definition: A measured or computed quantity with a value and, whenever the paper gives it, a unit.
exclude: a bare number with no named quantity

entity_types.name: conclusion
entity_types.definition: A proposition the paper asserts, that could in principle be true or false.
exclude: a restatement of a number without a claim
a hypothesis the paper explicitly rejects
surface_forms: the on-top divacancy is thermodynamically stable

instance_qualifiers.note: Two entities with the same surface form are NOT the same instance when one of these differs and the difference is stated. Mismatch forces must_not_merge.

cross_paper_rule: A shared generic term (for example 'monolayer WS2' or 'DFT') is evidence that both papers talk about the same KIND of object, never that they used the same physical sample, model instance, dataset, or experimental condition.
